findings.text: follow-on: the declared negative control does not reproduce at the reviewed head. The manifest's negative_control_note states that dropping one edge makes the node-minus-edge guard refuse with a RuntimeError (3 nodes, 1 edges) with EXIT=1, and the negative_control_log records that RuntimeError as the guard. At the reviewed head c36d828f2 neither holds: main() evaluates `join = edges[1]` (line 544) before the node-minus-edge guard (line 555), and the run's own negative-control-driver.py still unpacks the old three-tuple, so against the head file the driver dies first with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3, got 4)`. A corrected four-tuple edge-drop driver dies at line 544 with `IndexError: list index out of range`, still short of the guard. Either way the edge-drop mutation never reaches the guard at head, and the guard line the stored log names (469) locates it in the superseded initial commit b23118dcd, so the log documents the pre-fix revision rather than the reviewed one. The guard itself is sound: I falsified it by dropping a NODE instead of an edge (2 nodes, 2 edges -> `a contour tree does not have one more node than edge: 2 nodes, 2 edges`, EXIT=1). The control should be re-run against the head with a mutation the head code can carry to the guard.

follow-on: the head-arm gate log names the wrong revision. Its first line reads revision b23118dcd749977b77a987444d3cbc3c5f1808d4 -- the initial feature commit -- but its body carries the post-repair output only the c36d828f2 script produces (the third node is outside (virtual) with psi=virtual (no psi), plus the join level=+9.955e-04 Wb and class=diverted). At b23118dcd the same script printed a third node as minimum at R=+1.50258 Z=-1.20768 psi=+9.954762e-04 Wb. So the log was produced from a working tree carrying uncommitted fix changes and its declared revision is stale by one commit: a reader cannot tell which tree the numbers came from, and cannot use the log to confirm the reviewed head's behaviour without re-running it (I re-ran it; EXIT=0, byte-identical body).

follow-on: the "outside (virtual)" node is placed at the wall's MAXIMUM raw flux and reported with critical_type 0 (minimum), and the caption calls the region below the X-point the "private region". The node's own superlevel census shows the event at that level is a wall contact where a component DISAPPEARS as the level rises (census components fall 2 -> 1 between level +5.71e-04 and +1.43e-03, and the vanishing component is the wall-touching one), i.e. +9.9548e-04 Wb is a local maximum of psi on the wall, not a minimum; reporting critical_type 0 there reads, to a consumer applying the DD convention on raw psi, as a stationary minimum. Separately, in this reference psi just BELOW the X-point RISES from 0 at the saddle to +9.9548e-04 at the wall (verified: at R=1.50258, Z=-1.05 -> +2.35e-05, Z=-1.15 -> +4.46e-04, Z=-1.2077 -> +9.95e-04), so the region below the X-point carries positive psi and the caption's "private region below the X-point" names a position, not the conventional flux-below-the-saddle meaning. Not blocking: the class read (diverted) is defensible on the census and the receipt's flux_note does say the outside node is virtual; but the field names invite a minimum/private reading the numbers do not support.

gate_arms_note: The reviewed run is a figure node and its manifest carries no baseline_suite/after_suite gate-log arms, so added_failure_count and added_failure_ids are derived from an empty pair: added_failure_count 0, added_failure_ids []. The whole recorded gate surface is that empty sequence. I still reproduced what gate surface exists: the head arm (EXIT=0), the positive control inside the census (zero components above the axis), and a guard falsification of my own (dropping a node -> RuntimeError EXIT=1). That is not a suite, so it does not yield added_failure_ids.

justifications.durability: The figure is an artifact plus a generator, and the generator is the part that can rot: it depends on nova.equilibrium.analytic_single_null, nova.media and scripts.analytic_oracle_fixtures.measure.offset_wall, and it is committed under benchmarks/ with no test wired to re-run it, no CI step and no fixture that pins its numbers, so a change to any of those upstream modules moves the figure silently. The guards it does carry (the node-minus-edge check and the superlevel census) are in-process assertions on the generator, not on the committed PNG, and one of them was not shown to fire at head. The negative control lives only in the run directory and is itself stale, so nothing re-falsifies it later. Not lower because a drawing is legitimately an artifact rather than a guarded contract, and the receipt does make the numbers machine-checkable, but the checkability is unused.
justifications.evidence: The deliverable itself is real and reproducible: I ran the reviewed script against its own tree with output redirected to $TMPDIR (no write into the reviewed tree) and got EXIT=0 with nodes=3 edges=2 difference=1 sigma=1 and the same node/edge/class numbers the committed render.log carries. The receipt's census is internally consistent with the three-node path at every stated level (components 1/1/2/1/1/1/0/0 across the eight fractions), and the two positive-control levels above the axis are the check that an empty count is a real absence. The class read is sound: the probe level 5.71e-04 (between the saddle 0 and the contact 9.95e-04) carries two components, so the contact is reached through the saddle and can never be a limiter. But the two evidence records the deliverable ships are both stale relative to the tree they are supposed to document: the negative control was falsified against b23118dcd and cannot reach the guard at head c36d828f2, and the head-arm render.log's own first line names b23118dcd, not the reviewed head. Score reduced for two un-reproducible recorded controls, not for the physics.
justifications.fit: the deliverable follows the repository's evidence idiom: a benchmark script under benchmarks/, artifacts under docs/figures/contour-tree-topology-authority/explanatory/ with an SVG beside the PNG, and a landing fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/contour-tree-topology-authority/ whose img src is project-absolute (/nova/figures/...), as AGENTS requires, with the caption naming the wall's provenance (a constructed offset of the analytic separatrix, not a machine wall). Both commits are conventional with single-line subjects and substantive bodies, no AI attribution, no plan/sprint/ticket identifiers and no version suffix in any path, and the script speaks the plan's own vocabulary (critical_type, node/edge, class diverted). The one blemish is that the committed render.log's declared revision disagrees with the tree that produced its body. Score reduced one for habit -- the run log presents itself as the node's dated arm (line 2 revision/tree/cwd/module_file) but its own first line goes stale.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The dispatched goal -- section 1's explanatory figure -- is met. benchmarks/contour_tree_explanatory_figure.py renders one diverted single-null Solovev state (Cerfon-Freidberg reference) and commits it under docs/figures/contour-tree-topology-authority/explanatory/ as a PNG with an SVG beside it (both tracked, both present), with a JSON receipt and the run log. The figure follows the repository plotting rules: the poloidal panel is drawn with the axis off (no spines, ticks or gridlines), the scalar field is unfilled line contours on stated raw-flux levels in webers masked to the vessel (no filled contour, no colour map), the wall is drawn as its own unit, and both null kinds are marked through draw_nulls (a red triangle O-point at the axis, a red cross at the admitted saddle). Three nodes with node-count minus edge-count one are overlaid and each interior node is labelled directly with its critical type and flux in webers. Deduction: two of the figure's own annotations overstate what the receipt supports (the outside virtual node sits at a wall maximum; the region below the X-point has positive psi), recorded as a follow-on below.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 48a40fab1..c36d828f2 touches exactly the six declared write paths -- benchmarks/contour_tree_explanatory_figure.py, the four files under docs/figures/contour-tree-topology-authority/explanatory/ and the landing fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/contour-tree-topology-authority/ -- with nothing outside them; no source file under nova/ was touched, and the certificates, reference fixtures and analytic oracle are consumed read-only. Both commits are conventional with bodies, carry no AI attribution and no plan or ticket identifier. No stray tree and no writes in the reviewed worktree.
